name: Investor Permit for Non-Citizen Investors

requirements.blocker_text: Investment Fiji (formerly FTIB) investment-approval letter confirming shareholding structure, plus a Foreign Investment Certificate (FIC).

Minimum FJD 300,000 general investment threshold under the Investment (Reserved and Restricted Activities) Regulations 2022 (made under the Investment Act 2021); higher sector-specific thresholds apply (FJD 500,000 for retail/nightclubs-liquor bars outside hotel precincts/logging; FJD 1-2 million for fishing, tobacco manufacturing, homestay/backpacker accommodation, hotels/resorts, real estate).
requirements.fix_path: Secure the qualifying investment amount for the relevant sector.

evidence_required.document: Proof of capital transfer into Fiji

outcome.duration_length: 3 years (a separate 7-year Investor Permit category also exists per its own page title, but the fetched content did not disclose what distinguishes it -- disclosed as a gap, not modeled separately)

sources.title: Department of Immigration, Fiji -- Investor Permit for Non-Citizen Investors: requires Investment Fiji approval letter and Foreign Investment Certificate; investment minimum, duration confirmation, and fee not disclosed on this page

UNCTAD Investment Policy Monitor -- Fiji introduced a minimum investment threshold: FJD 300,000 general threshold effective 29 April 2022 under the Investment (Reserved and Restricted Activities) Regulations 2022 (Investment Act 2021), with higher sector-specific thresholds (FJD 500,000 / FJD 1-2 million); capital must be transferred within 3 months of incorporation (scheduled activities), balance within 1 year

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (Fiji). STATUS: DRAFT -- the investment-amount hard requirement is sourced only to UNCTAD (tier 2, corroborated independently by the US State Department's 2025 Investment Climate Statement for Fiji, also tier 2), not to a tier-1 government page directly -- immigration.gov.fj's own investor-permit pages do not disclose the minimum. GAP: Fiji's Investment Act 2021 delegates the actual schedule of 'reserved' (citizens-only) and 'restricted' (foreign-investment-above-threshold) activities to Cabinet-approved regulations reviewed every 2 years -- the current schedule itself (which specific sectors are reserved outright) could not be located at tier-1/2 in this pass; do not treat any specific sector as citizen-only without further sourcing. A separate '7-year Investor Permit' category exists by page title alone -- its distinguishing eligibility from the 3-year permit was not disclosed. Fiji has NO distinct work-independent/freelance route -- self-employed foreigners are channeled through this investor track, since operating a business requires Investment Fiji approval; that absence is confirmed, not a research gap.
